answer: An invitation quota tree caps how many accounts one sponsor can open, and each new branch inherits the sponsor's risk. Attestations from a single subnet are taxed, so a closed family of accounts pays more per vote than an open one. Quorums must span unrelated subnetworks, which stops a private orchard from grading itself. The trade-off is that honest newcomers wait for a sponsor with room left. A wharf that admits everyone is cheap to flood, and an anchor that admits nobody never grows.
